question: How well do large language models compress data of different modalities with arithmetic coding, and what does the compression view say about scaling laws, tokenization and in-context learning?
hypothesis: Since LLMs are strong predictors they should be strong general-purpose lossless compressors, and prediction and compression are equivalent in both directions.
contributions: Review how to compress with predictive models via arithmetic coding and connect it to language modeling research
Show LLMs reach strong compression rates on image and audio despite text-only training (Chinchilla 70B 43.4% ImageNet, 16.4% LibriSpeech)
Revisit scaling laws: dataset size is a hard limit on useful model size
Show tokenization is pre-compression that generally does not improve compression but packs more information into context

method.summary: Pretrained LLMs (Llama 2 7B, Chinchilla 1B/7B/70B) and small vanilla Transformers trained on enwik8 are used as probabilistic models inside an arithmetic coder to compress 1GB datasets of text, image and audio in 2048-byte chunks, compared with gzip, LZMA2, PNG and FLAC. Raw rate ignores model size; adjusted rate adds the float16 parameter bytes. Also sweeps model size and tokenizer, and uses gzip as a generative model.
method.task: offline lossless compression with arithmetic coding

datasets.name: enwik9
datasets.source: first 1e9 bytes of English Wikipedia XML dump of March 3rd 2006
datasets.preprocessing: ASCII mapping; lost bit appended to output

datasets.name: ImageNet
datasets.preprocessing: grayscale, flattened to 2048 bytes, each byte halved (lose LSB, appended)

datasets.name: LibriSpeech
datasets.preprocessing: int16 reduced to 1 byte, then halved to [0,127]; 2048 bytes is roughly 64 ms

models.name: Llama 2 (7B)
models.context: 2048 characters input, about 4 bytes per token coded

training.objective: log-loss (cross-entropy) on enwik8, equivalent to arithmetic-coding code length
training.tokens: inferred: 100 million bytes (enwik8), one byte per token

other.note: Only the small Transformers are trained; no training hyperparameters are given in the paper.

inference.decoding: arithmetic coding of model conditionals; for generation, one-step-ahead autoregressive sampling
inference.samples: Fig 4: 100 sequences averaged; generation examples: 3 samples per model for text
inference.prompting: no prompt; context is the preceding bytes of the 2048-byte chunk

other.image_generation: images 290x500; condition on first 250 pixels of each row, generate remaining 250

metrics.name: raw compression rate
metrics.definition: compressed size / raw size, excluding model parameters

metrics.name: adjusted compression rate
metrics.definition: (compressed size + model size at 2 bytes per parameter) / raw size, two-part code

eval.protocol: Single run reported; no seeds or confidence intervals; chunked (2048) and unchunked (infinity) settings for classical compressors.

availability.data: enwik9, ImageNet, LibriSpeech are public; Chinchilla not released

evidence.quote: We chose k = 100, which almost fully recovers the conditional distribution.

results.claim: Chinchilla 70B compresses ImageNet patches to 43.4% of raw size, beating PNG (58.5%).
results.setup: ImageNet 32x64 grayscale patches, 1GB, 2048-byte chunks, raw rate with arithmetic coding
results.quote: Chinchilla 70B, while trained primarily on text, compresses ImageNet patches to 43.4% and LibriSpeech samples to 16.4% of their raw size
results.note: Table 1 prints 48.0 for Chinchilla 70B ImageNet at chunk 2048 and 58.5 for PNG at chunk infinity (PNG chunked is 61.7); abstract's 43.4 and 16.4 do not match Table 1 (48.0, 21.0). Unexplained in the text.

results.claim: Chinchilla 70B reaches 16.4% on LibriSpeech, beating FLAC (30.3%).
results.quote: beating domain-specific compressors like PNG (58.5%) or FLAC (30.3%)
results.note: Table 1 gives 21.0 for Chinchilla 70B on LibriSpeech.

results.claim: Chinchilla 70B raw rate on enwik9 is 8.3%, versus gzip 32.3% and LZMA2 23.0% unchunked.
results.table: Table 1, row Chinchilla 70B, column enwik9 raw

results.claim: Adjusted for float16 parameter size, Chinchilla 70B scores 14008.3% on enwik9, far worse than gzip.
results.table: Table 1, row Chinchilla 70B, column enwik9 adjusted

results.claim: Small Transformers trained on enwik8 overfit to text: 3.2M gets 17.0% on enwik9 but 215.8% on ImageNet.
results.table: Table 1, row Transformer 3.2M, column ImageNet raw

results.claim: Compressing the float16 parameters of a 38M Transformer with gzip/LZMA2 barely shrinks them.
results.quote: we obtained rates of 92.2% and 89.1% on a 38M parameter Transformer with gzip and LZMA2

results.claim: Larger models compress larger datasets better but worse on smaller ones; each dataset size has an optimal model size once parameters are counted.
results.setup: Transformers trained on enwik8, evaluated on enwik7/8/9, adjusted compression rate (Fig 2)
results.quote: indicating that scaling laws are, in fact, dependent on the size of the test set

results.claim: Tokenization effect depends on model size: for the 200K model BPE 20K (19.3%) beats ASCII (22.9%), but for 38M ASCII (6.4%) beats BPE 20K (9.0%).
results.setup: enwik9, Transformers trained on enwik8, 38M parameters, ASCII vs BPE 20K

results.claim: gzip used as a generative model gives much noisier continuations than Chinchilla on text, image and audio.
results.setup: Qualitative; probabilities from 2^(l(x<i)-l(x<i b)); conditioning on half of each image row

results.claim: Compression rate falls quickly with sequence length, indicating in-context learning of data statistics.
results.setup: all subsequences of 2048 bytes averaged over 100 sequences; gzip, lzma, Chinchilla 1B, Transformer 4.8M
results.quote: indicating that the models learn some data statistics in-context, without any gradient-based training

limits: Context length limits offline compression to a few kilobytes; chunks of 2048 bytes were used and sliding was avoided for cost
Only offline two-part code adjusted rates; prequential (online) coding not evaluated since too costly
Chinchilla training data may conceivably contain encoded images or audio, authors say unlikely
Autoregressive generation looks only one step ahead, biasing gzip samples; no guarantee good compression yields good samples
Images are flattened and lose 2D correlations; bytes reduced to 7 bits via ASCII mapping
Transformer training hyperparameters, depth and width are not stated; single run, no seeds

terms.definition: compressed size / raw size, without counting model parameter size
compression rate that counts the parameter size (2 bytes per float16 parameter) as part of the compressed size
a model is trained on an external dataset before compressing a potentially different data stream, with fixed parameters
